intro: Exam-style performance-based tasks for Security+: controls, forensics, segmentation rules, cryptography, access control and vulnerability management.

questions.title: Categorize security controls
questions.scenario: Your policy review lists many controls. Sort each by its category (what it is) and its type (what it does).

activities.title: Sort by control category
activities.prompt: Drag each control to its category.

items.text: Badge reader on the server room

activities.title: Sort by control type
activities.prompt: Drag each control to the type that fits best.

items.text: Firewall rule that blocks a port

questions.explanation: Categories describe the implementation: technical (hardware, software), managerial (policy, risk), operational (people and process), physical. Types describe the effect: preventive stops it, detective finds it, corrective repairs it, deterrent discourages it (also directive, compensating).

questions.title: Order of volatility and risk math
questions.scenario: You are first on scene after a suspected breach, and later you must present the expected loss to management.

activities.title: Collect evidence from most to least volatile
activities.prompt: Order the sources of evidence, most volatile first.

activities.title: Quantitative risk
activities.prompt: An asset is worth $200,000. A flood would damage 25% of it and is expected once every two years (ARO 0.5).

rows.label: Formula for ALE (two terms, e.g. A x B)

questions.explanation: Collect the most volatile data first: registers and cache, RAM, swap and temp files, disk, remote logs, then archives. SLE = asset value x exposure factor = $200,000 x 0.25 = $50,000. ALE = SLE x ARO = $50,000 x 0.5 = $25,000.

questions.title: Screened subnet firewall rules
questions.scenario: A public web server (10.0.50.10) sits in a screened subnet and queries a database (10.0.60.20) inside the network. Admins work from 10.0.100.5. Replace the permissive rule set.

activities.title: Edit the rule set
activities.prompt: Edit, add, delete and reorder rules. Use Any, a single IP, or CIDR like 10.1.1.0/24. Ports can be a number, a range (8000-8080) or a list (80,443). Everything not allowed is denied. Requirements: the internet reaches the web server on HTTPS only; the web server may query the database on MySQL (TCP 3306); the admin workstation may use SSH to the database; everything else is blocked.

questions.explanation: Segmentation with least privilege: only the exact flows required are allowed (443 to the web server, 3306 from the web server to the database, SSH from one admin host), and the final implicit deny blocks the rest. The database must never be reachable directly from the internet.

questions.title: Symmetric, asymmetric and hashing
questions.scenario: A developer asks which cryptographic tool to use for each job. Sort the algorithms, then complete the key-usage facts.

activities.title: Sort the algorithms
activities.prompt: Drag each algorithm to its family.

rows.label: To digitally sign a message you use your ___ key
To verify that signature you use the sender's ___ key
A hash value proves this part of the CIA triad (one word)
Adding a unique salt to each password defeats precomputed ___ tables

questions.explanation: AES and 3DES use one shared key (symmetric). RSA, ECC and Diffie-Hellman use key pairs. SHA-256 and bcrypt are one-way hashes. A signature is created with the private key and verified with the public key; hashes provide integrity; salts defeat rainbow tables.

questions.title: Access control models and authentication factors
questions.scenario: Match the access scenario to the model, then classify the authentication methods by factor.

activities.title: Match the scenario to the access control model
activities.prompt: Drag each scenario to the model it describes.

items.text: The operating system enforces Secret and Top Secret labels
The file owner decides who can open the file
Permissions follow the user's job title
Access is allowed only from a managed device during business hours
A firewall ACL applies the same rules to every request

activities.title: Classify the authentication factors
activities.prompt: Drag each method to its factor.

questions.explanation: MAC uses labels set by the system, DAC lets owners decide, RBAC grants by role, ABAC evaluates attributes such as device and time, and rule-based control applies fixed rules to all. Factors: knowledge, possession, inherence (biometrics) and location.

questions.title: Vulnerability management
questions.scenario: Your scanner returned a list of findings. Rate them by CVSS v3 severity and put the remediation process in order.

activities.title: Match each CVSS score to its severity
activities.prompt: Drag each score to the right rating.

activities.title: Order the vulnerability management cycle
items: Analyze and prioritize by severity and exposure

questions.explanation: CVSS v3: 9.0 to 10.0 critical, 7.0 to 8.9 high, 4.0 to 6.9 medium, 0.1 to 3.9 low. Prioritize with severity, exploitability and asset value, fix or compensate, then rescan to confirm.
